method: Full441 lines across two pinned test files read, SHA256/Git blobs verified. Static test-to-implementation comparison; Jest suite not executed.
findings: customFetch tests cover initial success,429 then success,expired401 then success,network retry,400 failure,backoff and malformed/nonJSON500. They do not test failure of immediate post-refresh retry,Headers objects,aborts or ambiguous write completion.

400 alert test expects generic message while reviewed handleFinalError chooses Error: Bad Request when structured Spotify error exists. This is a source-level expected/actual mismatch; no Jest failure asserted without running suite.

400 handling invokes handleFinalError inside makeAttempt catch and again in outer retryFetch catch, potentially duplicating final analytics. First explicitly suppresses alert; outer may show structured alert. Test only checks alert and does not assert analytics call count.

Rate-limit test uses real2-second delay; several retry tests use real default delays, only explicit backoff test uses fake timers. Passing timing tests do not establish cancellation or deadline behavior.

Spotify API tests mock customFetch and check request shapes plus parsing/error categories. Delete responses are immediately fulfilled; no pending mutation or concurrency/snapshot conflict tests shown.

Empty successful response parsesnull in wrapper, but corresponding test uses JSON object. No interrupted/failed body read control seen in these files. Mock isolation does not qualify live API compatibility.
limits: No upstream Jest execution, external requests, liveAPI or browser runtime proof. pHash/ASAN deferred.
